acceptance: Red test first: sync-main on a tree whose only change is a loop quarantine move (tracked inbox item deleted, the same id under .evolve/inbox/quarantine/ untracked, the content equal apart from the loop's stamps) does not refuse, and main records the move.
Any other deletion or edit of a tracked inbox item still refuses.
Docs in STE: the sync-main section of the boundary docs records the rule.
fix: sync-main tolerates the loop's inbox stamps but treats the loop's own quarantine move as a foreign change, so the boundary stops at step 4 with the brake on until the console publishes the move by hand (PR #1234). Classify a quarantine move like a stamp: commit or carry the move as loop-owned inbox state, the same way consumed items are carried.
notes: Console route: boundary sync. Seen 2026-11-02 at the wave-148 boundary (landing-plans-reconcile-with-adr-0147).
source: console, 2026-11-02, wave-148 boundary stopped at sync-main
summary: A loop quarantine move of an inbox item makes evolve sync-main refuse, which stops the whole boundary and keeps the brake on.
title: sync-main carries the loop's own inbox quarantine move instead of stopping the boundary
